proposedCases.feasibility: Concrete bounded next implementation; not executed.
steps: Start healthy installed QA build; finish readiness and seed durable gameplay/settings saves. Require current builtin or a healthy downloaded bundle and no pending update. Snapshot both saves, current/fallback metadata, pending/high-water and active bundle tree hashes.

Provision empty 256 KiB private tmpfs using existing mount namespace guards; verify real app can write there and truncate owned target to zero. Serve a fresh correctly signed ZIP with sequence above high-water; hold its response before headers/body.

After server observes ZIP GET, find exactly one new files/temp_<id>.tmp matching newly registered downloading bundle. Require length zero, absence from baseline, and no other active download. Cleanup has already occurred before HTTP getResponseCode. Replace only this owned empty temp path with relative link to bounded target. Verify resolved path from app namespace; no existing saved game file is changed.

Fill only bounded tmpfs to ENOSPC, confirm real app write error and distinct capacity. Release HTTP gate; capture actual DownloadService write failure, controller result, unchanged current bundle/pending/high-water and gameplay/save availability.

After native request settles, remove only the exact owned link if it remains; plugin may remove it during failure cleanup. Unmount via keeper. Retry identical manifest sequence/hash/version through controller, verify staging, next-launch activation, save preservation and normal cold boot.

proposedCases.feasibility: Concrete candidate without plugin modification; cross-volume move and alternate reporting preflight required.
steps: Resolve exact task app data container and Documents; keep Library and all current/fallback bundles untouched. Capture Documents inventory; mount overlays original directory without deleting or moving its existing files. Avoid any concurrent document import/export.

Prepare 8 MiB HFS+ image; first prove a small real native cross-volume FileManager move succeeds (Filesystem.rename implementation must be checked) while there is space. If it fails EXDEV/EACCES instead, stop: no ENOSPC claim.

Start signed update request on normal filesystem; hold ZIP response after GET proves the plugin disk-space preflight passed. Mount bounded filesystem at this task app Documents path only; verify mount identity/capacity. Use Library-owned status files or in-memory outcome, since normal Debug report Documents/native-probe.json is temporarily covered.

Fill bounded filesystem using guarded hard-cap loop. Release response. Normal URLSession transient ZIP stays on its ordinary app temporary path; storeDownloadedFile must move/copy it into the full bounded Documents path. Capture native disk-full error and independent kernel ENOSPC. This qualifies download staging, not network streaming disk writes.

Observe gameplay/process survival and unchanged Library saves/current metadata. Wait for request completion, unmount, verify original Documents inventory/save bytes, and retry identical publication normally through real controller.
caveats: Do not mount all Library: it would cover saves and active/fallback bundles. Do not replace package_<id>.tmp with a symlink because plugin removes it before move.
Small volume mounted before request tests preflight rejection, not actual write ENOSPC. It may be a separate optional case.
Mounting a task-owned Documents overlay is broader than the prior save symlink test; exact app ownership, reporting route, no concurrent I/O, and restoration must be proven before execution.

proposedCases.feasibility: Needs Debug debugger coordination proof; filesystem polling alone is unsafe and not sufficient.
steps: Download a valid signed archive completely on ordinary app storage. Use a normal Debug breakpoint immediately before extraction creates/writes its first entry: Android CapgoUpdater.unzip overload receives random dest; iOS saveDownloaded/first extractZipEntry exposes destUnZip/destPath.

While stopped before first file write, read exact random extraction directory from debugger. Require app-root prefix capgo_unzip_, newly created/empty state, and no current/pending/fallback reference. Mount only that owned extraction directory onto bounded filesystem (256 KiB Android private namespace or8 MiB iOS HFS+); preserve original empty directory. Never redirect an archive entry outside its canonical root or disable ZIP traversal checks.

Before resuming, configure debugger to stop again on thrown error before native recursive cleanup if needed. Use large first regular entry and leave one filesystem block free so file creation succeeds and payload write reaches ENOSPC. Archive padding, if needed, is finite (for example16 MiB zeros), added only to a copied QA bundle before normal signing; no unbounded ZIP bomb.

Resume and capture actual native extraction outcome, filesystem free bytes/kernel diagnostic, app survival, current bundle and durable saves. On iOS explicitly detect FileHandle exception/crash. Android generic unzip error requires path/kernel evidence because cause is discarded.

Coordinate unmount before native recursive cleanup crosses mounted root when necessary; never let test cleanup delete unrelated bundle directories. Retry exact publication after recovery, verify staging/activation and saves. If debugger unavailable under existing normal Debug permissions, report unqualified rather than racing folder creation or weakening security.

nativeSourceEvidence.finding: Transfer failure stores status error with empty checksum.
Extraction failure stores status error after checksum has already been calculated. Nonempty checksum cannot reliably identify startup failures.
Native download already supports retry of failed/deleted/deleting matching versions through its own targeted cleanup. JS controller does not broadly delete error records.
Watchdog stores lastFailedBundle then marks current error; autoDeleteFailed may change it to deleting/deleted and remove files.
Android watchdog similarly persists lastFailedBundle, marks error, rolls back, and schedules native cleanup.
getFailedUpdate consumes native record before JS durable save; iOS equivalent at4774. Not used to avoid destructive-read crash window.

implementation.saveAllowlist: Existing src/platform/native-storage.ts:14 accepts trials.nativeUpdates prefix; test verifies new key is allowed.
implementation.behavior: Immediately before native set/reload, record native bundle ID and release version then await durable flush. Transfer/extraction failures before activation create no journal entry, so identical signed publication can retry. A failed start leaves its journal entry through native rollback/auto-deletion and blocks even a higher sequence or changed hash reusing that version. Existing durable sequence high-water remains unchanged.
implementation.healthyRemoval: After successful native notifyAppReady, remove only journal entry whose native ID and version equal current healthy bundle, then flush. Removal/read/flush errors do not reject successful native acknowledgement or block gameplay.
implementation.bounds: Maximum32 unique versions per native/runtime namespace and16KiB serialized ledger. Malformed or oversized history blocks new updates; full history rejects new downloads/activations. Failure entries are never evicted to create capacity. A new native-version namespace begins fresh.
implementation.unchanged: Native cleanup retains ownership of error/deleting/deleted files; no broad deletion, getFailedUpdate call, credentials, QA configuration, or app reload scheduling change.
implementation.legacyDevelopmentLimitation: No store app has shipped. Historical development watchdog failures predating journal creation remain protected by sequence high-water for that publication, but lack durable version quarantine against higher-sequence reuse after native metadata deletion. No speculative migration or destructive native failed-record read was added.
